Here's a pretty good deal, with free shipping:

https://www.budsgunshop.com/catalog/product_info.php/products_id/70953

The Axis is a cut-corners cheaper version of the venerable Savage 10/110, which is their flagship short action rifle line. In my eyes, the biggest failing of the Axis is that the action has no intrinsic recoil lug, and instead there's a slot in the receiver where the action recoils onto a notch in the stock. This immediately limits you severely in terms of stock choices and makes for a weaker action.

Since the difference in price is like $100 (or you could even get a used Savage Model 10 for the same price as an Axis), it's worth it to get a Model 10/110 instead for a variety of reasons:

  • Accustock (if you get a new one)
  • HUGE aftermarket
  • Available in an enormous number of variations (barrel lengths, barrel thicknesses, stock types, finishes, safety types, with/without irons, you name it)
  • Much more easily repairable and has greater spare parts availability, the Savage Mod 10 has been an American mainstay for over half a century
  • Higher quality fit and finish overall, much nicer finishing work especially on the bolt/receiver area which leads to a smoother, quieter pull

That said, the Axis is not a bad rifle. It will put bits of lead where you point them, in a reliable fashion. Just, in my opinion, it's worth the extra hundred bucks or so to get the real-deal Savage and be done with it.
